title: constraint-annotations.json — per-child SGDC/SDC annotations (authored by the stage from the reaped child reports)
description: What each child's RTL implies for the constraint files, in the child's REAL module names so `sync_cell -name` matches the netlist. The lint-cdc and synthesis agents read this to fill scripts/constraints.sgdc and the SDC exceptions. Kept separate from rtl-files.json because simulation consumes only the file layout: bundling them would invalidate simulation on an annotation-only edit. Every category is present with an explicit empty array when a child has none — an omitted category and 'none' are not the same claim. Nothing in this stage verifies that a reported module name is real: lint-cdc writing `sync_cell -name` into the SGDC is the first place a wrong name surfaces. Shape only is checked here; that every manifest child has an entry is checked by finalize, against the manifest.

sync_cell.description: Module names of custom synchronizers this child authored.

reset_synchronizer.description: The synchronized-reset NETS this child drives out of a reset synchronizer — not the synchronizer module's name. SGDC's two synchronizer commands take different kinds of name: sync_cell takes the module, reset_synchronizer takes the net, and giving it a module name is a Fatal that aborts rule checking for the whole run (measured on vL-2016.06). The net is named in the scope that instantiates the synchronizer, so it is that child's to declare, not the one that wrote the module.

set_case_analysis.description: Test-control ports held at a constant during analysis.

quasi_static.description: Signals that cross domains but change only at configuration time.

create_generated_clock.description: Divider/PLL outputs this child generates: the module and the pin the clock leaves on. clocks.json marks the clock `generated` and defers the pin to here.
